updates.name: Daniel D. Richter
updates.bio: Theodore S. Coile Distinguished Professor of Earth and Climate Sciences in Duke's Nicholas School of the Environment. His soils research treats soil as part of Earth's deep Critical Zone and asks how land use reshapes it over decades to millennia. He has directed South Carolina's Long-Term Calhoun Soil-Ecosystem Experiment, a USDA Forest Service collaboration, since 1988.
updates.research_interests: soil change under land use; Critical Zone science; deep-profile soil biogeochemistry of carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus and trace elements; long-term soil-ecosystem experiments; the Anthropocene

updates.name: Arthur J. Miller
updates.bio: Distinguished Research Oceanographer Emeritus and Senior Lecturer in Climate Sciences at Scripps Institution of Oceanography, UC San Diego, with a 1986 Scripps doctorate in physical oceanography. A Fellow of the American Meteorological Society; current projects on the CV include the California Current Ecosystem LTER and inner-shelf data assimilation.
updates.research_interests: ocean modeling, predictability and data assimilation; coupled ocean-atmosphere models; dynamics and ecosystem response of the California Current; Pacific decadal variability; long-period tides, tsunamis and barotropic normal modes

updates.name: Michael R. Landry
updates.bio: Distinguished Professor of Oceanography at Scripps Institution of Oceanography, UC San Diego, in the biological oceanography curriculum group of the Ocean Biology Program, with his research administered through the Integrative Oceanography Division. Listed topics are plankton ecology and food webs, marine microbiology, population and community ecology, and biological effects of climate change.
updates.research_interests: food-web interactions of micro- and mesozooplankton; plankton population and community ecology; physical-biological coupling

updates.name: Peter Franks
updates.bio: Emeritus biological oceanographer in the Integrative Oceanography Division at Scripps Institution of Oceanography, UC San Diego, trained in the MIT-Woods Hole doctoral program. The profile describes work linking physics and biology from micro- to mesoscales through analytical and numerical models, including phytoplankton production at fronts, internal waves and turbulence, and harmful algal blooms.
updates.research_interests: coupled physical-biological dynamics across micro- to mesoscales; analytical and numerical modeling of physics-biology interactions; phytoplankton productivity in fronts, internal waves and turbulent flows; harmful algal blooms and red tides
updates.current_affiliation: Integrative Oceanography Division, Scripps Institution of Oceanography, UC San Diego
